name: Husham
overview: Husham was a male Edomite king who succeeded Jobab as ruler over Edom. He is noted specifically as coming from the land of the Temanites, a region associated with the Edomite people. His role as king places him within the historical lineage of Edomite leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Husham appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. There are no additional titles or meanings recorded beyond his identification as king of Edom.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Husham as a descendant of Esau, connecting him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this ancestral link, there are no further family relationships recorded in the biblical text for Husham.
scriptureSignificance: Husham's significance lies in his position as a king of Edom, marking a continuation of the Edomite monarchy after Jobab. His association with the Temanites situates him within a notable region of Edom, reflecting the ongoing governance and tribal structure of Esau's descendants. Through this, Husham contributes to the biblical record of Edomite rulers, which is part of the broader narrative of the nations descending from Esau.
